chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Uthman ibn Abd al-Malik al-Hadrami from Abu Bakr al-Hadrami who said:
Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said to me: 'O Abu Bakr, everything upon which the sun shines is pure.'

key_terms.أَبُو جَعْفَرٍ: Abu Ja'far, referring to Imam Muhammad al-Baqir (peace be upon him)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on the purity of things exposed to sunlight in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) establishes a foundational principle in Shia jurisprudence that anything exposed to the sun is ritually pure (tahir), serving as the default state for objects unless proven otherwise. This narration is pivotal in the debate between the schools of thought regarding whether impurity is intrinsic or requires specific evidence, reinforcing the concept of 'asl al-taharah' (primordial purity). It provides jurists with a clear criterion for determining the purity of surfaces and items in daily worship and ritual ablution.
